docs.title: Fast backendsin Dart
docs.text:
Dox is a web backend framework for Dart, like Laravel. Routing, an ORM, migrations, validation, auth and a CLI come in one place. It runs one isolate per CPU core and builds to a small native binary.

Get started GitHub

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
You need Dart 3.13 or newer.

dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.1   # install the CLI
dox create new_blog                          # make a new project
cd new_blog && dox s                         # start the server

docs.title: Why Dox
docs.text:
• Fast by default

    One isolate per CPU core and streamed bodies. dox build makes an AOT native binary. See Performance.

  • ORM and query builder

    Models, relations, migrations and transactions for Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite. See Database.

  • Typed validation

    Schemas like Zod with dox_validation, or rule strings with req.validate().

  • OpenAPI

    Make OpenAPI 3.1 docs and a Swagger UI page with dox_openapi.

  • File storage

    Local disk and S3 behind one API with dox_storage.

  • Cache

    Memory, file and Redis cache with dox_cache.

  • Real time

    Events with WebSocket or Socket.IO.

  • Security

    JWT authentication, CORS, encryption and hashing.

  • CLI

    Create projects, controllers, models and migrations, and build for production. See Dox CLI.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Dox talks to Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite with the dox_orm package.

  • Query builder: build SQL with methods.
  • Models: one class per table.
  • Transactions: many queries that succeed or fail together.
  • Migration and Schema: create and change tables.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The query builder and models live in the dox_orm package.

dart pub add dox_orm

import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

Note

dox_orm was called dox_query_builder before 3.0. The old package only re-exports dox_orm now. Change your pubspec.yaml and imports to dox_orm.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
Put the connections in lib/config/database.dart. connection is the name of the default connection.

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: Env.get('DB_CONNECTION', 'postgres'),
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 5432,
      user: 'postgres',
      password: 'postgres',
      database: 'postgres',
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'maxConnectionCount': 10},
      debug: false,
    ),
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql, // also for MariaDB
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 3306,
      user: 'root',
      password: 'password',
      database: 'dox',
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'maxConnectionCount': 10},
      debug: false,
    ),
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: 'storage/app.db', // file path, or ':memory:'
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);

Start it in a service, so every isolate has its own pool.

class ORMService implements DoxService {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }
}

docs.title: .env
docs.text:
The app config and the migration commands read these values.

DB_CONNECTION=postgres # postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432           # 3306 for mysql
DB_NAME=dox            # for sqlite: the file path, like storage/app.db
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres

MySQL extra options

maxConnectionCount (default 10) is the pool size. collation (default utf8mb4_general_ci), timeoutMs, timeZone and maxConnectionAge are also read. The MySQL 8 default login (caching_sha2_password) works, also without TLS. Without TLS the driver asks the server for its RSA key to encrypt the password. To not ask, give the key in serverPublicKey, or set useSSL: true. Set allowPublicKeyRetrieval: false to turn the asking off.

SQLite extra options

busyTimeout (default 5000 ms) is how long a query waits for a lock.

Table and column names are quoted

Table and column names you pass to select, where, join, groupBy, orderBy, insert and update are quoted: "name" on Postgres and SQLite, and `name` on MySQL. So names like order or key work. table.column, * and column as alias are handled. A value with ( (for example count(*) as total) is kept as it is. For anything else, use the raw functions (selectRaw, whereRaw, joinRaw). On Postgres a quoted name is case sensitive, so userId is not the same as userid.

docs.title: MySQL and MariaDB
docs.text:
• The driver is mysql_dart. MySQL 8 and 9 login (caching_sha2_password) works.
  • It has a real connection pool and sends values as bound parameters.
  • getDatabaseConnection() returns a MySQLConnectionPool.
  • CREATE, ALTER and DROP save right away. A transaction can not undo them.

docs.title: MySQL JSON
docs.text:
Info

On MySQL, JSON columns are decoded to Map or List when you read them. Other text columns are not decoded. MariaDB stores JSON as LONGTEXT, so the driver can not see the column type. On MariaDB, text that starts with { or [ and is valid JSON is decoded. boolean() columns (TINYINT(1)) are read as bool.

docs.title: MySQL types
docs.text:
Info

MySQL values are converted by column type: integers to int, FLOAT, DOUBLE and DECIMAL to double, DATE, DATETIME and TIMESTAMP to DateTime (read as UTC), boolean() (TINYINT(1)) to bool. TIME stays a String.

docs.title: SQLite
docs.text:
SQLite is good for development, tests and small apps. For a busy production app, use Postgres or MySQL.

How it runs

The sqlite3 package calls SQLite directly (FFI). A query blocks the isolate while it runs. Each isolate has one connection. While a transaction is open, other queries of that isolate wait. The database file uses WAL mode, so readers do not wait for the writer. busy_timeout makes a query wait for a lock from another isolate instead of failing. Foreign keys are turned on.

Types

SQLite has no bool, JSON or date type. boolean() is saved as 0/1 and read back as bool. json() is saved as text and read back as Map or List. Dates are saved as ISO text in UTC and read back as DateTime. This uses the type in CREATE TABLE, so it works on tables made by Schema or by SQL with the same type names (BOOLEAN, JSON, TIMESTAMP, DATE, DATETIME). The driver finds the type by the table names in the query. A column with an alias (active as is_active) is not converted.

Limits

  • schema.table with .change() changes a column (type, null, default) by making the table again and copying the rows. It keeps the primary key, foreign keys, unique columns and indexes. It throws for tables with CHECK constraints or generated columns.
  • dropColumn does not work on a primary key, unique or indexed column (SQLite limit).
  • A new column with NOT NULL needs a default value.
  • truncate() runs DELETE FROM and resets the id counter.
  • insertMultiple with rows that have different keys inserts the rows one by one, because SQLite has no DEFAULT in VALUES.
  • There is no RIGHT JOIN before SQLite 3.39.

Native library

The sqlite3 package (v3) bundles SQLite with a build hook. You do not install a system library. dart run and dart test run the hook by themselves. For the AOT binary use dox build (it runs dart build cli). It puts the library in build/bundle/lib/, next to build/bundle/bin/server. Keep the two folders together. dart compile exe does not work with build hooks. See Deployment.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
A migration changes your database schema step by step: create a table, add a column, and so on. Each migration has an up (do the change) and a down (undo it).

Write migrations in Dart with the schema builder. The same migration then works on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite. Plain .sql migrations still work too.

docs.title: Create a migration
docs.text:
dox make:migration create_users_table

This makes db/migration/2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart:

import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}

The name gives the start of the file:

Name File starts with create_users_table schema.create('users', ...) and dropIfExists('users') add_avatar_to_users_table schema.table('users', ...) in up and down any other name empty up and down

create:migration is the old name of the same command.

Raw SQL and data in a Dart migration

schema.driver runs raw SQL on the same connection and transaction: await schema.driver.execute("UPDATE users SET role = 'admin' WHERE id = 1"); Do not use models or QueryBuilder in a migration. They use another connection.

docs.title: The registry
docs.text:
Dart can not load a file at run time in an AOT build. So Dox keeps a list of your Dart migrations in db/migration/migrations.dart:

// Made by `dox make:migration` and the `dox migration:*` commands.
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

import '2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart' as m1;

final List<MigrationEntry> migrations = <MigrationEntry>[
  MigrationEntry(
    '2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table',
    m1.CreateUsersTable(),
  ),
];
  • dox make:migration and every dox migration:* command write this file again. You do not edit it.
  • It finds each file named YYYY_MM_DD_HHMMSS_name.dart and its class ... extends Migration.
  • The name of a migration is its file name without .dart. The order is by name.

The first dox make:migration also makes bin/migrate.dart in your app:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await Migrator(migrations: migrations).run(args);
}

The dox migration:* commands run dart run bin/migrate.dart <command>. So your migrations run as part of your app code.

docs.title: Run migrations
docs.text:
Command What it does dox migration:run Run the migrations that did not run yet. Short name: dox migrate. dox migration:rollback Undo the last batch. dox migration:rollback --step=2 Undo the last 2 migrations, even across batches. dox migration:reset Undo all migrations. dox migration:refresh Undo all migrations, then run them again. dox migration:status Show each migration, its batch, and if it ran.

migrate:rollback, migrate:reset, migrate:refresh and migrate:status are short names.

A batch is the group of migrations that ran in one migration:run. Migrations are undone newest first. The ran migrations are saved in the dox_db_migration table.

When a migration fails, the error shows its name, and the command exits with code 1. The failed migration is not saved, and the later ones do not run.

You can also run dart run bin/migrate.dart run (or rollback --step=2, reset, refresh, status) yourself.

docs.title: Run on server start
docs.text:
The AOT server binary can run the migrations, because the registry is compiled in:

import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Migrator(migrations: migrations).migrate();
  await Dox().startServer();
}

Keep the db/migration folder next to the binary if you also have .sql migrations.

docs.title: Database settings
docs.text:
The migrations use the .env file in your project. When there is no .env file (for example in Docker), they use the environment variables.

DB_CONNECTION=postgres # or mysql (also MariaDB), or sqlite
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=postgres
DB_USERNAME=admin
DB_PASSWORD=password

For SQLite, only two variables are needed:

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_DATABASE=storage/app.db # file path, made if missing

Info

The default port is 5432 for postgres and 3306 for mysql. One run uses one database connection.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Each migration runs in one transaction. On Postgres and SQLite, a failed migration undoes all its changes.

MySQL

On MySQL and MariaDB, CREATE, ALTER and DROP save right away. So if a migration fails half way, these changes stay. Only data changes are undone. Keep each MySQL migration small: one table change per migration.

To run a migration without a transaction (for example CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on Postgres):

class AddSearchIndex extends Migration {
  @override
  bool get withinTransaction => false;
  ...
}

SQLite foreign keys

On SQLite, foreign key checks are off while a migration runs. This lets Dox make a table again (see SQLite notes). Before the end, Dox checks all foreign keys. The migration fails if one is broken.

docs.title: SQL migrations
docs.text:
A .sql migration is still fine. Use it for SQL that only one database understands.

dox make:migration create_blog_table --sql

-- up
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blog (
    id serial PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
);

-- down
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS blog
  • Put the up SQL under a line -- up, and the down SQL under a line -- down. Each of these lines must be on its own line. Other -- lines are normal SQL comments.
  • Statements are split on ;. A ; inside quotes, comments or a postgres $$ ... $$ body does not split.

SQLite ids

In SQLite, id serial PRIMARY KEY does not make an auto increment id. The id stays NULL. Use id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT for SQLite. table.id() in Dart does this for you.

docs.title: Dart and SQL in one folder
docs.text:
Both kinds can live in db/migration. They run in file name order (the timestamp).

  • With bin/migrate.dart: the Migrator runs the Dart migrations from the registry and reads the .sql files from the folder, merged by name.
  • Without bin/migrate.dart (a project with only .sql files): dox runs the .sql files itself, like before.
  • A Dart and a .sql migration with the same name is an error.

docs.title: Upgrade from Dox 2
docs.text:
• Migration() is now Migrator(). Migration is the base class of a Dart migration.
  • Migrator().migrate(connection) is now Migrator(connection: connection).migrate().
  • rollback(null, 2) is now rollback(step: 2).
  • Schema.create(...) is now Schema().create(...) (or the schema given to up). See the schema builder.
  • make:migration makes a Dart file. Use --sql for a .sql file.
  • Old .sql migrations keep their names, so they do not run again. You can turn one into a Dart file with the same name. It will not run again either.

docs.title: Query Builder
docs.text:
The query builder makes SQL for you. You chain methods, and Dox runs the query with bound values. It works on Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite.

  • Set up the database first: see Database.
  • For transactions, see Transactions.

Changes in 3.x

  • Table and column names are quoted. On Postgres, userId is not the same as userid any more.
  • orderBy throws an ArgumentError when the direction is not asc or desc.
  • toSql() wraps the where part in brackets.
  • count() ignores limit, offset and orderBy. With groupBy it returns the number of groups.
  • See the upgrade guide for all changes.

docs.title: Schema builder
docs.text:
The schema builder creates, changes and drops tables. The same code works on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite. You mostly use it inside a migration.

await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
  table.id();
  table.foreignId('user_id').constrained().cascadeOnDelete();
  table.string('title');
  table.text('body').nullable();
  table.enumeration('status', <String>['draft', 'published']).defaultTo('draft');
  table.timestamps();
});

docs.title: Get a schema
docs.text:
In a migration, up and down get a Schema. It runs on the migration connection.

Outside a migration, Schema() uses the query builder connection. You can also give a driver: Schema(driver).

Schema schema = Schema();
await schema.dropIfExists('posts');

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: Method What it does create('t', (Table table) {...}) Create table t. It fails when the table exists. table('t', (Table table) {...}) Change table t: add columns, change columns, keys. drop('t') Drop table t. It fails when the table is missing. dropIfExists('t') Drop table t when it exists. rename('from', 'to') Rename a table. hasTable('t') true when the table exists. hasColumn('t', 'c') true when the column exists. getColumnListing('t') The column names, in order.

Helpers:

  • timestamps(): nullable created_at and updated_at (timestampTz).
  • softDeletes([deleted_at]): nullable deleted_at (timestampTz), for SoftDeletes models.
  • rememberToken(): nullable remember_token VARCHAR(100).
  • morphs('owner'): owner_id (unsigned big integer), owner_type (string) and an index on both.

JSON on SQLite

SQLite has no JSON type. The column is declared as JSON, so the SQLite driver knows to decode it when you read it.

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text:
Modifiers come after the column type. They can be chained: table.string('email').nullable().unique().

Modifier What it does Notes nullable() Allow NULL. Columns are NOT NULL by default. nullable(false) makes it NOT NULL again. defaultTo(value) Default value. Strings are escaped, so any text is safe. bool, numbers, null, Map/List (saved as JSON) and DateTime work too. withDefault is the old name. defaultRaw('sql') Default as raw SQL. It is not escaped. Put expressions in ( ): defaultRaw('(1 + 1)'). MySQL and SQLite need it. useCurrent() Default to the current time. Same as defaultRaw('CURRENT_TIMESTAMP'). useCurrentOnUpdate() Set the current time on each update. MySQL only. Postgres and SQLite ignore it. Set the time in your code there. unique() Add a unique index {table}_{column}_unique. index() Add an index {table}_{column}_index. primary() Make the column the primary key. unsigned() UNSIGNED. MySQL only. Others ignore it. comment('text') Column comment. Postgres and MySQL. SQLite ignores it. after('column') Put the new column after another one. MySQL only, only in schema.table. Others add it at the end. change() Change an existing column (in schema.table). See Change columns.

MySQL defaults on TEXT and JSON

MySQL only allows a default on TEXT, BLOB and JSON as an expression. The schema builder writes it as DEFAULT ('value') for you.

docs.title: Change a table
docs.text:
await schema.table('users', (Table table) {
  table.string('avatar').nullable().after('email'); // add
  table.string('name', 100).nullable().change();    // change
  table.renameColumn('bio', 'about');
  table.dropColumn('age');
  table.dropColumns(<String>['a', 'b']);
});

A column in schema.table is added. Add .change() to change a column that exists.

docs.title: Change columns
docs.text:
change() sets the full new column: type, null, default and comment. Give every modifier you want to keep.

// before: string('title') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'x'
table.string('title', 500).nullable().defaultTo('x').change();

How it runs:

Driver SQL Postgres One ALTER TABLE: ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... USING col::type, SET/DROP NOT NULL, SET/DROP DEFAULT, and the enum CHECK again. MySQL ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN <full column>. SQLite SQLite can not change a column. Dox makes the table again (see below).

change() with unique() or index() adds the index. It fails when the index already exists.

docs.title: Indexes and keys
docs.text:
columns is a column name or a list of names.

table.index(<String>['state', 'created_at']);  // posts_state_created_at_index
table.unique('slug');                          // posts_slug_unique
table.primary(<String>['post_id', 'tag_id']);  // composite primary key

table.dropIndex(<String>['state', 'created_at']); // by columns
table.dropUnique('posts_slug_unique');            // or by name

Index names are {table}_{columns}_{index|unique|foreign}. You can give your own name as the last argument: table.unique('slug', 'my_name').

docs.title: Foreign keys
docs.text:
table.foreignId('user_id').constrained().cascadeOnDelete();
// same as:
table.foreignId('user_id');
table.foreign('user_id').references('id').on('users').onDelete('cascade');
  • constrained([table], [column = 'id']) guesses the table from the column: user_id becomes users, category_id becomes categories. Dox models use singular table names by default (User is user). If your table is singular, give it: constrained('user').
  • Actions: onDelete('cascade' | 'set null' | 'restrict' | 'no action'), onUpdate(...), and the short ones cascadeOnDelete(), nullOnDelete(), restrictOnDelete(), cascadeOnUpdate().
  • Put nullable() before constrained(): table.foreignId('editor_id').nullable().constrained('users').
  • Drop it: table.dropForeign(<String>['user_id']) or table.dropForeign('posts_user_id_foreign').

Same type on both sides

id() is a big integer. foreignId() is a big integer too, so they match. If the parent uses increments() (a normal integer), use unsignedInteger() for the child on MySQL.

docs.title: SQLite notes
docs.text:
SQLite ALTER TABLE can only add, rename and drop columns. For these changes, Dox makes the table again:

  • change() of a column,
  • foreign(...) on an existing table,
  • dropForeign(...).

It makes a new table with the change, copies the rows, drops the old table and renames the new one. It keeps the columns, primary key, AUTOINCREMENT, foreign keys, indexes and enum checks. All of it runs in one transaction. It fails on tables with other CHECK constraints or with generated columns.

Other SQLite limits:

  • primary(...) on an existing table is not supported.
  • A new column that is NOT NULL needs a default. A new column can not default to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
  • dropColumn fails when the column is in an index or a foreign key. Drop those first.

docs.title: Per driver notes

CHECK (col IN (...)) unsigned ignored UNSIGNED ignored comment COMMENT ON COLUMN inline COMMENT ignored after ignored AFTER col ignored useCurrentOnUpdate ignored ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ignored change() ALTER COLUMN MODIFY COLUMN table rebuild add/drop foreign key on a table ALTER TABLE ALTER TABLE table rebuild schema changes in a transaction yes no, saved right away yes index name length 63 64 no limit

docs.title: See the SQL
docs.text:
Every change is a Table blueprint. A grammar turns it into SQL, without a database:

Table table = Table('users', creating: true)
  ..id()
  ..string('email').unique();
print(table.toSql(PostgresGrammar()));
// [CREATE TABLE "users" ("id" BIGSERIAL NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, "email" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL),
//  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "users_email_unique" ON "users" ("email")]

Grammars: PostgresGrammar, MysqlGrammar and SqliteGrammar. On SQLite, the changes that need a table rebuild only run on a database.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
A transaction runs many queries as one. Either all of them are saved, or none.

  • It commits when the function ends.
  • It rolls back when the function throws. The error is thrown again.

docs.title: Use
Connections
docs.text:
• Postgres and MySQL use a connection pool. Set the size with maxConnectionCount in the connection extra config.
  • A transaction uses one connection of the pool. Other queries use the other connections.
  • SQLite has one connection per isolate. While a transaction is open, other queries of that isolate wait.
  • Values are always sent as bound parameters. They are never written into the SQL text.

Changed in 3.x

Before 3.x, Postgres ran every query in its own transaction. Now a query only runs in a transaction when you use QueryBuilder.transaction().

docs.title: Hide column
Computed values
docs.text:
A computed value is a getter that is added to toJson() and toMap(). It is like $appends with an accessor in Laravel.

Add @Computed() to a getter in the model, then run dart run build_runner build.

@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column(name: 'first_name')
  String? firstName;

  @Column(name: 'last_name')
  String? lastName;

  @Computed() // json key: full_name
  String get fullName => '$firstName $lastName';

  @Computed(name: 'initials') // custom json key
  String get shortName => '${firstName?[0]}${lastName?[0]}';
}

User? user = await User().find(1);
print(user?.toJson());
// {id: 1, first_name: John, last_name: Wick, ..., full_name: John Wick, initials: JW}
  • The default key is the getter name in snake_case (fullName becomes full_name).
  • A computed value is never a column. It is not read from the database, and it is not sent in INSERT or UPDATE.
  • hidden also hides computed values. Use the json key, for example ['full_name'].
  • Computed values of loaded relations are in the nested json too.
  • toMap(original: true) returns the raw database row, so it has no computed values.

Performance

The code is made by build_runner. There is no reflection. A model without @Computed() does no extra work in toJson(). A getter runs each time toJson() or toMap() is called, so keep it fast.

Casts

Dox has no $casts list. The field type does the cast: DateTime? is parsed from the database, and a JSON column can be a Map<String, dynamic>? or List<dynamic>? field. For other conversions, use the beforeSave and beforeGet hooks of @Column.

docs.title: Model events
docs.text: A model fires events when you save, delete or restore it. You can run your own code on these events. There are two ways: hooks in the model, and observer classes.

docs.title: Hooks in the model
docs.text:
Override an on... method in the model. Then run dart run build_runner build.

@DoxModel(softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? email;

  @override
  Future<void> onCreating() async {
    email = email?.trim().toLowerCase();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> onDeleted() async {
    await AuditLog().create({'message': 'user $id deleted'});
  }
}

Info

The hook names start with on (onCreating, not creating). This is because created and deleted are common column names. Declare the hooks in the model class itself. The generator looks there.

docs.title: Events and order
docs.text:
Call Events, in order save() on a new model saving → creating → INSERT → created → saved save() on a loaded model saving → updating → UPDATE → updated → saved create({...}) the same as save() on a new model delete() deleting → DELETE or soft delete → deleted forceDelete() forceDeleting → deleting → DELETE → deleted → forceDeleted restore() restoring → UPDATE deleted_at = NULL → restored

The model hook runs first. Then the observers run, in the order you added them.

Query updates and deletes fire no events

Events fire only on a model instance. User().where('active', false).update({...}), User().where(...).delete() and insertMultiple() run one query and fire no events. This is the same as Laravel.

docs.title: Cancel an operation
docs.text:
Throw CancelModelEvent in a "before" event (saving, creating, updating, deleting, forceDeleting, restoring). The query does not run. save(), delete(), forceDelete() and restore() return false.

@override
Future<void> onDeleting() async {
  if (isAdmin == true) throw CancelModelEvent('admins can not be deleted');
}

bool deleted = await user.delete(); // false

create({...}) returns the unsaved model (its id is null) when an event cancels it. Any other error from a hook is thrown to the caller.

docs.title: Observers
docs.text:
An observer is a class that listens to one model. Override only the methods you need. Each method gets the model.

class UserObserver extends ModelObserver<User> {
  final Mailer mailer;

  UserObserver(this.mailer);

  @override
  Future<void> created(User user) async {
    await mailer.sendWelcome(user.email!);
  }
}

Add it once, for example when the app starts:

Model.observe<User>(UserObserver(mailer));
  • You can add more than one observer to a model.
  • Model.forgetObservers<User>() removes the observers of User. Model.forgetObservers() removes all.

docs.title: Skip events
docs.text:
await user.saveQuietly(); // save without events

await Model.withoutEvents(() async {
  await user.save();
  await post.delete();
});

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Hooks run inside the transaction of the caller. save() does not start a transaction by itself.

  • If an "after" hook (created, saved, ...) throws, the row is already written.
  • To undo the row when a hook fails, wrap the call in QueryBuilder.transaction():
await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  await user.save(); // if onCreated() throws, the INSERT is rolled back
});

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• There is no reflection. The generator sets hasModelHooks only for models that declare a hook.
  • A model with no hooks and no observers does no event work. It is one bool check, plus one map lookup when some other model has observers.
  • When a model has events, create({...}) fills a model with fromMap() and calls save(). Only the @Column fields are saved then.

docs.title: Usage
BelongsTo
docs.text:
A "belongs-to" relationship is a fundamental concept in database modeling. Consider a scenario where we have a Comment model associated with a User model. In this case, we define a method called user within the Comment model. This user method invokes the BelongsTo method and returns its output. This relationship signifies that a comment belongs to a particular user.

In practical terms, this means that each comment in our database is linked to a single user. When we want to retrieve the user associated with a specific comment, we can use the user method, making it easy to access user information for that comment. This BelongsTo relationship helps establish connections between records in a meaningful way, enhancing the organization and retrieval of data in our database system.

BelongsTo Class Structure 
class BelongsTo {
    final Type model;
    final String? foreignKey;
    final String? localKey;
    final Function? onQuery;
    final bool? eager;

    const BelongsTo(this.model,
        {this.foreignKey, this.localKey, this.onQuery, this.eager});
}

docs.title: ManyToMany
docs.text:
A "many-to-many" relationship is a powerful concept in database design, often used to represent complex associations between entities. Consider a scenario where we have an Artist model and a Song model. To represent the fact that each artist can have multiple songs, and each song can have multiple artists, we establish a "many-to-many" relationship.

To achieve this, we typically create an intermediary table, often referred to as a "pivot" or "junction" table, which contains foreign keys referencing both the Artist and Song models. This table captures the relationships between artists and songs.

ManyToMany Class Structure 
class ManyToMany {
    final Type model;
    final Function? onQuery;
    final bool? eager;
    final String? localKey;
    final String? relatedKey;
    final String? pivotForeignKey;
    final String? pivotRelatedForeignKey;
    final String? pivotTable;

    const ManyToMany(
        this.model, {
        this.eager,
        this.onQuery,
        this.localKey,
        this.relatedKey,
        this.pivotForeignKey,
        this.pivotRelatedForeignKey,
        this.pivotTable,
    });
}

However, you have the flexibility to provide a custom name to the pivotTable parameter if needed.

Cache
docs.text:
Cache() stores data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast. It runs on dox_cache, which is built into dox_core.

Drivers: file, memory, redis and null (stores nothing).

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
config/cache.dart:

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: Env.get('CACHE_STORE', 'file'),
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': Env.get('REDIS_HOST', '127.0.0.1'),
      'port': Env.get<int>('REDIS_PORT', 6379),
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);

Pass it to AppConfig(cache: cache). Each store is made once per isolate, the first time you use it.

Many isolates

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate has its own memory store. Use redis when all isolates and servers must see the same data.

Redis options: host, port, username, password, db, tls, prefix.

docs.title: Values are JSON
docs.text: Values must be JSON types: Map, List, String, num, bool. A Map comes back as Map<String, dynamic>.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
// no duration: the value stays forever
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().get('foo');             // 'bar', or null
await Cache().get('foo', 'default');  // a default when it is missing
await Cache().has('foo');             // true
await Cache().forget('foo');
await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});
await Cache().flush();                // remove all items of the store

docs.title: remember
docs.text:
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () => Post().all(),
);

The value is read from the cache. When it is missing, the function runs and its result is stored. rememberForever(key, fn) does the same without expiry.

docs.title: store
docs.text:
await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().store('memory').get('foo');

docs.title: tag
docs.text:
await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Never run production with dart run

dart run (and dox serve) uses the JIT compiler. It is made for development. It uses about 25x more memory at start (around 390 MB instead of 16 MB) and starts slower. Always build an AOT binary for production.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Compile the app to a native binary (AOT).

dox build

This makes a build/bundle/ folder:

File What it is build/bundle/bin/server the native binary. No Dart SDK needed to run it build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (eg. SQLite) build/bundle/db/ your migrations, run at start build/bundle/.env.example copy it to build/bundle/.env, or use env variables

dox build runs build_runner first (when your app uses it). Then it runs dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build. It exits with code 1 when a step fails, so CI can stop.

Not dart compile exe

dox_orm depends on sqlite3 v3. It bundles SQLite with a build hook. dart compile exe does not run build hooks, so it stops with an error. dart build cli is the same AOT compiler and runs the hooks. Keep bin/ and lib/ together: the binary loads the libraries from ../lib.

Start the application.

cd build/bundle
./bin/server

The binary reads .env and db/ from the folder you start it in. A real environment variable wins over the .env file.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The Dockerfile in a new Dox app is a multi-stage build:

  1. The dart:stable image builds the AOT bundle with dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build.
  2. The final image is FROM scratch. It holds only the Dart AOT runtime files (/runtime/ from the dart image), the bundle (/app/bin/server and /app/lib/), db/ and an empty /tmp.
FROM dart:stable AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get
COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline
RUN dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
RUN dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r db /out/app/db

FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]

The image has no .env file, so secrets stay out of it. Pass config as environment variables.

docker build -t my-app .
docker run -p 3000:3000 -e APP_PORT=3000 -e APP_KEY=... -e DB_HOST=... my-app

Or use env_file: .env in docker-compose.yml.

docs.title: HTTPS: put a proxy in front
docs.text:
Do not serve HTTPS from Dart. TLS in Dart's HttpServer is slow (a known Dart SDK issue). Dox has no bindSecure.

Run Dox on plain HTTP on a private port. Put Caddy or nginx in front of it. The proxy does TLS, HTTP/2 and gzip.

Then tell Dox to trust the proxy, so req.ip() and req.scheme() show the real client:

AppConfig(
  /// the proxy's IP, or a range like '10.0.0.0/8', or '172.16.0.0/12' for docker
  trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'],
);
  • req.ip() reads X-Forwarded-For. Dox walks the list from the right and skips your proxies, so a fake value from the client is ignored.
  • req.scheme() reads X-Forwarded-Proto (http or https). req.isSecure() is true for https.
  • trustedProxies is empty by default. Then Dox ignores those headers, because any client can send them.
  • ['*'] trusts everyone. Only use it when the app port is not reachable from outside.

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
Caddy gets a certificate for you and sets X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. Websockets work with no extra config.

example.com {
  encode gzip
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
upstream dox {
  server 127.0.0.1:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
  default upgrade;
  ''      '';
}

server {
  listen 443 ssl http2;
  server_name example.com;

  ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

  # match maxMultipartSize in AppConfig
  client_max_body_size 100m;

  gzip on;
  gzip_types application/json text/plain text/css application/javascript;

  location / {
    proxy_pass http://dox;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;

    # websocket upgrade
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;

    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

    # stream uploads to Dox, do not buffer them in nginx first
    proxy_request_buffering off;
  }
}

server {
  listen 80;
  server_name example.com;
  return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

docs.title: Keep it running
docs.text:
Dox uses all CPU cores by default (see Isolate).

  • When a worker isolate dies, Dox prints the error and starts it again.
  • When the main isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code. Let a supervisor restart it: restart: unless-stopped in Docker compose, or Restart=always in systemd.
# /etc/systemd/system/dox.service
[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/srv/app/build/bundle
ExecStart=/srv/app/build/bundle/bin/server
EnvironmentFile=/srv/app/build/bundle/.env
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: Many processes or machines
docs.text:
One Dox process already uses every core. You only need more processes to run on more machines, or to restart one process without downtime. Run each one on its own port (or machine) and list them in the proxy:

upstream dox {
  server 10.0.0.11:3000;
  server 10.0.0.12:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

Websocket rooms then need a shared adapter (like Redis), because each process has its own memory.

docs.title: Dox CLI
docs.text:

Run dox help to see all commands. Run dox help <command> for one command.

docs.text:

Export bin path

Please make sure you have included bin path to your profile. If you did not added path to your profile yet, open ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc and paste below line.

export PATH="$PATH":"~/.pub-cache/bin"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Env.get() reads a value from the environment or from the .env file.

The environment wins

A real environment variable (set in the shell, Docker or systemd) wins over the .env file. So you can keep .env for development and use real variables in production. Before 3.x, only the .env file was read.

Example 
Env.get('APP_KEY');

// With default values
Env.get('APP_KEY', 'default_value');

docs.title: With type
docs.text:
IntStringBoolNullable 
Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000)

Env.get<String>('APP_KEY')

Env.get<bool>('SOCKETIO_ENABLED', false) // true, 1, yes, on

Env.get<String?>('AWS_BUCKET') // null when it is not set

docs.title: Missing values
docs.text:
A missing or empty key gives the default. With no default:

  • String gives an empty string ''. It is never the text "null".
  • String? and dynamic give null.
  • int, num, double and bool throw an ArgumentError with the key name. A value that is not a number throws too.

APP_KEY

When APP_KEY is empty and APP_ENV=production, Dox().startServer() stops with an error. In other environments it logs a warning. Make a key with dox key:generate.

docs.title: File Storage
docs.text:
Storage() saves and reads files on a disk: the local folder, AWS S3 (and R2, MinIO, Spaces), or memory. It runs on dox_storage, which is built into dox_core.

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
config/storage.dart:

StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: Env.get('STORAGE_DISK', 'local'),
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': 'https://app.test/files', // for url() and signedUrl()
    },
    's3': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 's3',
      'bucket': Env.get('AWS_BUCKET'),
      'region': Env.get('AWS_DEFAULT_REGION', 'us-east-1'),
      'key': Env.get('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID'),
      'secret': Env.get('AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'),
      'endpoint': Env.get('AWS_ENDPOINT'), // R2, MinIO, Spaces
    },
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
  },
);

Pass it to AppConfig(storage: storage).

Driver Options local root (default storage), url, app_key (default: your APP_KEY), visibility s3 bucket, region, key, secret, token, endpoint, path_style (MinIO), url (CDN), visibility, acl, batch_delete memory none. For tests

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
// save with a new uuid file name, returns '/images/<uuid>.png'
String path = await Storage().put('images', bytes, extension: 'png');
String path2 = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', file);

Uint8List? bytes = await Storage().get(path);  // null when missing
bool found = await Storage().exists(path);
await Storage().delete(path);

String url = await Storage().url(path);         // needs the disk `url` option
String signed = await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10));

// another disk
await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports', bytes, extension: 'pdf');

putRequestFile on the local disk moves the upload temp file. It does not read it into memory.

docs.title: stream and download
docs.text:
Route.get('/photo', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().stream(req.input('path'));    // shown in the browser
});

Route.get('/report', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().disk('s3').download('reports/2024.pdf'); // saved as a file
});

Both read the file as a stream, from any disk, with Content-Length. A big file is never loaded into memory. A missing file answers 404.

// routes/web.dart
Route.files('files');                    // GET /files/{key*}, signed URLs only
Route.files('public', signed: false);    // any file of the disk

String url = await Storage().signedUrl('invoices/1.pdf'); // https://app.test/files/invoices/1.pdf?expires=...&signature=...

A missing, wrong or expired signature answers 403. Set the disk url option to the full URL of the route (https://app.test/files).

Disk fake = Dox().storage.fake('s3');
await uploadReport();
expect(await fake.exists('reports/2024.pdf'), isTrue);

Implement DriverContract from dox_storage and register it, for example in a service:

Dox().storage.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver());
await Storage().disk('dropbox').put('notes', bytes, extension: 'txt');

docs.title: Isolate
docs.text: Dox runs your HTTP server on many isolates (threads) at once. All of them listen on the same port (HttpServer.bind(..., shared: true)), and the OS spreads the connections between them.

docs.title: How many
docs.text:
By default Dox starts one isolate per CPU core (Platform.numberOfProcessors). So one process uses the whole machine.

To change it, set totalIsolate in lib/config/app.dart, or set APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE in the environment.

totalIsolate: Env.get<int>('APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE', Platform.numberOfProcessors),

Use fewer isolates when:

  • the machine also runs the database or other heavy work, or
  • you run websocket rooms without a Redis adapter. Each isolate has its own memory, so a room only reaches clients on the same isolate. Use 1 then.

docs.title: What each isolate does
docs.text:
Each isolate has its own memory. At start, every isolate:

  1. runs the setup() of each service in services (for example it opens its own database pool),
  2. registers the routes and form requests.

This is cheap: it happens once at start, not per request. Keep setup() light. Open connections there, but do not load big data into memory, because it is loaded once per isolate.

docs.title: When an isolate crashes
docs.text:
• An error in a request is caught. Dox sends a 500 and keeps going.
  • A stray async error (for example a future that nobody awaits) is caught and passed to errorHandler. The isolate keeps running.
  • If a worker isolate still dies, Dox prints [dox] isolate N exited, restarting with the error to stderr, and starts a new one after 1 second.
  • If the main isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code. Let your supervisor (Docker restart:, systemd Restart=always) start it again. See Deployment.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
The short version:

  1. Build with dox build and run the AOT binary. Never dart run in production.
  2. Put Caddy or nginx in front for HTTPS and gzip.
  3. Keep the default isolates (one per CPU core).
  4. Keep the body limits on. Uploads stream to disk.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Measured on a MacBook (Apple M-series, 8 cores), Dart 3.13. The load tool ran on the same machine, so it took some of the CPU. Treat the numbers as a comparison, not as a max.

json = GET /json returning a small map. param = GET /user/{id}. 64 keep-alive connections, 8 seconds.

Setup Start Idle memory json req/s param req/s JIT, 1 isolate 1.0 s 388 MB 26-28k 29k AOT, 1 isolate 0.05 s 16 MB 27-30k 26-28k JIT, 8 isolates 1.0 s 398 MB 54-57k 52-58k AOT, 8 isolates 0.05 s 16 MB 60k 56-62k

Before and after the changes in this release (AOT):

Test Before After json, 1 isolate 23k/s 27-30k/s param, 1 isolate 20k/s 26-28k/s json, 8 isolates 54k/s 60k/s param, 8 isolates 52k/s 56-62k/s 50 MB upload, peak memory 1,100 MB 72-93 MB 50 MB upload, JIT peak memory 1,380 MB 389 MB (= JIT idle) request logs on, req/s cost -13% -4%

For reference, a bare dart:io server with the same JSON gives about 44k/s on one isolate. So Dox adds some cost on top of dart:io, and that is the next place to look.

Run it yourself (from packages/dox-core):

bash benchmark/run.sh          # SECS=10 CONNS=64 N=<cores> to change

It needs only Dart and curl. It uses a small Dart load tool (benchmark/load.dart), because wrk and oha are often not installed.

docs.title: Request body limits
docs.text:
Dox reads a body while it streams in, and stops once it is too big. It answers 413 Payload Too Large. It checks Content-Length first, so a big upload is refused before one byte is read. It also counts bytes while reading, so a client that sends no Content-Length (chunked) is stopped too.

AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in the proxy (client_max_body_size in nginx).

docs.title: File uploads
docs.text:
• A file up to 1 MB stays in memory.
  • A bigger file is written to a temp file while it arrives. A 50 MB upload no longer needs 1 GB of RAM.
  • The temp file is deleted when the response is done. So save it before you return from the controller.
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');           // to storage (a cheap move on local disk)
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4');
await file.bytes;     // whole file in memory. avoid for big files

docs.title: Big responses
docs.text:
Return a Stream<List<int>> or a File. Dox pipes it to the client and does not load it all into memory.

Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

A File response sets Content-Type (from the file name), Content-Length and Accept-Ranges. It answers Range: bytes=... with 206 Partial Content, so video players can seek and downloads can resume.

Storage().stream() and Storage().download() on the local disk also stream the file and send Content-Length.

JSON and text responses are encoded once, straight to bytes, with Content-Length set.

docs.title: gzip
docs.text:
gzip in Dart is off by default.

AppConfig(compress: true);
  • It saves bandwidth, but costs CPU on every response, in the same isolate that serves requests.
  • A proxy (Caddy, nginx) does it better. Turn it on in Dart only when there is no proxy.
  • With compress: true, text and JSON responses are sent chunked, without Content-Length, because dart:io only gzips when the length is not set.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
LogMiddleware prints one JSON line per request. Writing to stdout blocks. Dox now collects log lines and writes them every 20 ms (or every 64 KB) in one write. If the process is killed hard, the last 20 ms of request logs can be lost. Errors from Logger are still written right away.

Turn LogMiddleware off when a proxy already writes access logs.

docs.title: What else was fixed on the hot path
docs.text:
• Routes are grouped by method, and each route's regex is built once, not on every request.
  • Route params are now per request. Before, two requests to the same route at the same time could see each other's params.
  • The controller's argument types are read once per controller, not three times per request.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: If your application requires additional services like a database, auth etc.., you'll need to create a class that implements the DoxService interface and then register it with Dox. Since Dox operates with isolates (multi-threading), these extra services must be passed to each isolate to ensure their availability on all isolates.

docs.title: Example with auth
Services
Integration test
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:test/test.dart';

String baseUrl = 'http://localhost:${config.serverPort}';

void main() {
    setUpAll(() async {
        Dox().initialize(appConfig);
        await Dox().startServer();

        // for for few seconds to fully started http server
        await Future<dynamic>.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: 500));
    });

    test('/api/ping route', () async {
        var url = Uri.parse('$baseUrl/api/ping');
        var response = await http.get(url);
        expect(response.statusCode, 200);
        expect(response.body, 'pong');
    });
}

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text:
dox_websocket adds a WebSocket server to the Dox HTTP server. Use it for live chat, notifications and other real-time updates.

Want Socket.IO clients?

Use Socket.IO. Turn it on with AppConfig(socketIo: SocketIoConfig(enabled: true)). It runs on the same port, works with the official Socket.IO clients, and has acks and namespaces. dox_websocket keeps working next to it.

docs.title: 1. Create websocket service with redis adapter
docs.text:
class WebsocketService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Redis sub = Redis();
    Redis pub = sub.duplicate();

    WebsocketServer io = WebsocketServer(Dox());
    io.adapter(WebsocketRedisAdapter(
      subscriber: sub,
      publisher: pub,
    ));
  }
}

Many isolates need Redis

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core by default. Each isolate has its own memory. Without an adapter, a room only reaches clients on the same isolate.

  • Use the Redis adapter. It needs ioredis ^2.0.0-alpha.1.
  • Or set totalIsolate: 1 in lib/config/app.dart (or APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1).

docs.title: 2. Register websocket service to dox app/config/services.dart
docs.text:
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[
  ... /// other services
  WebsocketService,
];

docs.title: 3. Create websocket controller
docs.text:
dox create:controller SocketController -ws

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_websocket/dox_websocket.dart';

class ChatWebSocketController {
  intro(WebsocketEmitter emitter, dynamic message) {
    // sent message to chart room but exclude the sender
    emitter.room('chat').emitExceptSender('intro', message);
  }

  noti(WebsocketEmitter emitter, dynamic message) {
    // sent message to chart room including the sender
    emitter.room('chat').emit('noti', message);
  }
}

Note

As webSocket maintains an open connection, there is no requirement to send back any values from your controller method.

docs.title: 4. register websocket route and events
docs.text:
ChatWebSocketController controller = ChatWebSocketController();

Router.websocket('ws', (WebsocketEvent event) {
    // when client sent an event called `intro`, 
    // it will execute `controller.intro` method
    event.on('intro', controller.intro);

    // when client sent an event called `noti`, 
    // it will execute `controller.noti` method
    event.on('noti', controller.noti);
});

Info

You can register websocket routes on lib/routes/web.dart or you can also create custom websocket router and register in lib/config/app.dart. Both option will create a websocket url on ws://127.0.0.1:{port}/ws.

Note

You also have the option to register WebSocket routes for multiple paths, rather than just the default /ws route.

docs.title: Client Usage
docs.text: You have the option to utilize either the built-in browser WebSocket or any WebSocket library for clients. The key requirement is that when sending data, it must be in the form of a JSON string containing both event and message attributes. Refer to the example below for clarification.

docs.title: Example with Dart
docs.text:
import 'dart:io';

// The event name that is listening in your routes
// Eg. DoxWebsocket.on('intro', controller.intro);
String event = 'intro';

// Message can be any type such as int, float, map, string etc..
String message = "Mingalaba!"; 


// Encoding to json formatted string
var data = jsonEncode({
    "event": event,
    "message": message,
});

String url = 'ws://localhost:3000/ws';
WebSocket socket = await WebSocket.connect(url);

socket.add(data);


// If you would like to join the room, please use event name `joinRoom`
var joinRoomData = jsonEncode({
    "event": "joinRoom",
    "message": "chat", // sent room name as message
});

// Sent message to join the chat room
socket.add(joinRoomData);

docs.title: Example with javascript
docs.text:
For Handling with javascript, we suggested you to use below library. https://github.com/dartondox/dox-web-socket-client

import DoxWebsocket from '@dartondox/websocket';

const socket = DoxWebsocket('ws://127.0.0.1:3000/ws', {
  maxRetries: 18, retryAfter: 2000 
})

socket.onConnected(() => {
  console.log(socket.id)
})

socket.onError(() => {
  console.log('socket error')
})

// Listen in client for intro event that will sent from the server
socket.on('intro', (msg) => {
  console.log(msg)
})

socket.onClose(() => {
  console.log('socket closed')
})

function sendMessage(message) {
  socket.emit('intro', message)
}

docs.title: room
docs.text:
Set the room before emit to client

emitter.room('chat').emit('event-name', message);

Info

Use the same name the client sent with joinRoom. room() returns a new emitter. The room does not stay set for later events.

docs.title: emit
docs.text:
Emit to all the client connected to the same websocket route.

emitter.emit('event-name', message);

docs.title: emitExceptSender
docs.text:
Emit to all the client connected to the same websocket route except the sender.

emitter.emitExceptSender('event-name', message);

docs.title: Release (maintainers)
docs.text: All public packages are published to pub.dev by the Release GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/publish.yaml). It runs when you push a tag like v3.0.0-alpha.1. It uses pub.dev automated publishing, so no token or secret is needed.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the new version in the root pubspec.yaml, for example version: 3.0.0-alpha.1.
  2. Run the script. It copies the version to every package, to every sibling dependency (^3.0.0-alpha.1), and to the CLI version constant. 
    bash bin/update_versions.sh
  3. Add a ## 3.0.0-alpha.1 entry to each package CHANGELOG.md (pub.dev warns if it is missing).
  4. Commit and push. 
    git commit -am "release 3.0.0-alpha.1"
git push
  5. Wait until the Test workflow is green for this commit. The release workflow does not run the tests.
  6. Tag and push the tag. This starts the publish. 
    git tag v3.0.0-alpha.1
git push origin v3.0.0-alpha.1

The workflow first checks that the tag matches the root version and every package version. Then it publishes in this order: dox_annotation, dox_builder, dox_orm, dox_query_builder, dox_migration, dox_core, dox_auth, dox_websocket, dox_validation, dox_openapi, dox_storage, dox_cache, dox_socketio, dox. A package is skipped when that version is already on pub.dev. So if a run fails halfway, fix the problem and click "Re-run jobs". It continues where it stopped.

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text: Open Actions > Release > "Run workflow". It runs dart pub publish --dry-run for every package and publishes nothing. Warnings (for example a missing CHANGELOG entry) are shown as yellow warnings and do not fail the run.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
On pub.dev, for each package (dox_annotation, dox_builder, dox_orm, dox_query_builder, dox_migration, dox_core, dox_auth, dox_websocket, dox_validation, dox_openapi, dox_storage, dox_cache, dox_socketio, dox):

  1. Open https://pub.dev/packages/<name>/admin.
  2. Under "Automated publishing", click "Enable publishing from GitHub Actions".
  3. Repository: dartondox/dox.
  4. Tag pattern: v{{version}}.
  5. Tick "Require GitHub Actions environment" and set the environment to pub.dev.
  6. Save.

On GitHub, in dartondox/dox > Settings > Environments, create an environment named pub.dev. Optional: add yourself as a required reviewer, and limit it to tags v*. The old PUB_CREDENTIALS secret is no longer used.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
• 3.x deploys by itself. The Docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yaml) runs on every push to develop that changes docs/, mkdocs.yml or the workflow. It runs mike deploy --update-aliases 3.x latest.
  • 2.x deploys by hand. Open Actions > Docs > "Run workflow", pick version 2.x. It builds from the v2.x branch (change it with the ref input).
  • After each deploy, the workflow writes small redirect pages for the old root links, the root index.html, a 404.html and the CNAME file. So dartondox.dev and old links keep working.
  • The workflow pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN. If gh-pages is a protected branch, add a PUSH_TO_PROTECTED_BRANCH secret with a token that may push to it.

docs.title: Why mike
docs.text:
• Old docs stay online at /2.x/, and readers switch with the version menu.
  • Each version is built once from its own branch. A new deploy does not touch the other versions.
  • Old links from before versioning are kept with redirect pages, so search results and blog posts still work.

docs.title: New major version
docs.text: When 4.x starts, deploy 4.x with mike deploy --update-aliases 4.x latest. Keep a v3.x branch, and add 3.x to the workflow input, so 3.x can still be fixed.
