docs.title: v3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
New packages

  • dox_orm: the new name of dox_query_builder.
  • dox_validation: typed schemas, coercion, custom rules, JSON Schema.
  • dox_openapi: OpenAPI 3.1 as JSON and YAML, Swagger UI.
  • dox_storage: local, S3 and memory disks, signed URLs.
  • dox_cache: memory, file and Redis cache with tags and locks.
  • dox_socketio: Socket.IO v4 server with a Redis adapter.

Database

  • SQLite support.
  • MySQL uses mysql_dart with a real pool. MySQL 8 login works.
  • Postgres uses a real pool.
  • QueryBuilder.transaction().
  • whereNull, whereNotNull, whereNotIn, orWhereIn, orWhereNotIn, selectRaw, boolean() column.
  • Table and column names are quoted.
  • Fixed: model.delete() deleted every row. orWhere returned soft deleted rows. MySQL update() changed nothing.
  • whereIn and orderBy no longer put user values into the SQL.

Migrations

  • MySQL and SQLite.
  • Rollback undoes only the last batch. New --step, migration:reset and migration:refresh.
  • A failed migration stops the run.

Core

  • Uploads over 1 MB stream to a temp file. A 50 MB upload needs about 75 MB of memory, not 1.1 GB.
  • Body limits answer 413.
  • File responses stream, with Range support.
  • One isolate per CPU core by default. A crashed isolate restarts.
  • trustedProxies for X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto.
  • Faster router.
  • dox build makes a native binary. The Docker image is about 11 MB.
  • Fixed: CORS preflight, cookie Max-Age, RequestFile.size, validation of missing fields, websocket rooms.

Auth

  • Fixed: a login with only a password could match the first user.

Full notes: release PR #112.

docs.title: Cache (dox_cache)
docs.text:
dox_cache is a cache like Laravel Cache. It has remember, tags, atomic locks and four drivers.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_cache for Cache(). In a Dox app, set the stores in config/cache.dart (the CacheConfig of this page), and use Cache(). Dox().cache is the CacheManager. Cache().repository is the CacheStore. This page is for the full API and for using dox_cache outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_cache

import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';

Note

dox_core exports CacheConfig, CacheManager, CacheStore and CacheLock from this package. They are the same classes, so importing both packages is fine.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Driver What it is Shared between isolates memory a map in this isolate. Fast. Optional LRU size limit No file one JSON file per key in a folder Yes (same machine) redis Redis, with the ioredis package Yes null stores nothing. Use it to turn caching off -

Warning

Dox runs many isolates. Each isolate has its own memory cache. Use redis when isolates or servers must see the same data.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app:'},
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store

Redis options: host, port, username, password, db, tls, prefix.

docs.title: Basic use
docs.text:
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
await store.get('a');               // 1
await store.get('missing', 'none'); // 'none'
await store.has('a');               // true
await store.forget('a');

No ttl means forever

put without a ttl keeps the value forever. (The old Cache() in dox_core keeps it for 1 hour.) A zero or negative ttl removes the key.

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
Get the cached value, or run the function and cache the result.

List<dynamic> posts = await store.remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 10), () async {
  return await loadPostsAsJson();
});

docs.title: All methods
docs.text: Method What it does get(key, [default]) the value, or the default when missing or expired put(key, value, [ttl]) store it add(key, value, [ttl]) store only when missing. Returns true when stored has(key) true when the value is not null forget(key) remove it. Returns true when it was there flush() remove all items of this store many(keys) / putMany(map, [ttl]) many keys at once increment(key, [by]) / decrement(key, [by]) change a number. A missing key starts at 0. The ttl stays forever(key, value) store without expiry remember(key, ttl, compute) see above rememberForever(key, compute) the same, without expiry pull(key) get it, then remove it tags([...]) a tagged view lock(name, [ttl]) an atomic lock

docs.title: Values are JSON
docs.text:
Values must be JSON types: Map, List, String, num, bool, null. Other types throw.

  • A Map comes back as Map<String, dynamic>. A List comes back as List<dynamic>.
  • A stored null reads as a miss. has returns false for it.
  • For a model, store model.toJson(), not the model.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
await store.tags(<String>['users']).put('u1', 'Ann');
await store.tags(<String>['users']).flush(); // removes only the 'users' items

Tags work with every driver. Old items are not deleted right away. They are just not found any more, and they go away when their ttl ends.

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Only one worker runs the code at a time.

CacheLock lock = store.lock('report', Duration(seconds: 10));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    // only one worker runs this
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

bool got = await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5)); // wait up to 5 seconds

memory and redis support locks. The memory lock works inside one isolate only.

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text:
Every store has a prefix (default dox_cache:). It is added to every key. Use different prefixes when two apps share one Redis database.

Redis flush

flush deletes only the keys with the prefix. It never runs FLUSHDB. An empty prefix makes flush throw.

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver()); // or add a ready driver

MyDriver extends CacheDriver and implements get, put, add, increment, forget and flush.

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text: dox_openapi makes an OpenAPI 3.1 document for your Dox app. You get openapi.json, openapi.yaml and a Swagger UI page at /docs.

docs.title: In a Dox app
docs.text:
dox_core has it built in. Add an OpenApiConfig to AppConfig:

// config/openapi.dart
OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  servers: <Server>[Server('https://api.example.com')],
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()},
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'AuthMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[<String, List<String>>{'bearerAuth': <String>[]}],
  },
);

AppConfig(openApi: openApi, ...);
  • GET /docs (Swagger UI), GET /openapi.json and GET /openapi.yaml are added after your routes.
  • enabled is null by default: the docs are on only when APP_ENV is development or local. So production is off unless you set enabled: true. When it is off, there is no extra work per request.
  • Every route is added. The document is built on the first /docs request, and again when routes change.
  • Request bodies come from the route body: option, or from the form request of the controller (schema() first, then rules()):
Route.post('/posts', controller.store, body: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'title': v.string().min(3),
}));

// or: store(PostRequest req) where PostRequest has schema() or rules()
  • Middleware names come from the route groups and router middleware (preMiddleware), so securityByMiddleware knows which routes need a login.

docs.title: Write the files: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and openapi.yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder

It runs bin/openapi.dart of your app:

// bin/openapi.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}

writeOpenApi runs your services and registers the routes. It does not start the server.

The rest of this page is for describing routes by hand, and for using dox_openapi outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_openapi

import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

docs.title: 1. Describe your routes
docs.text:
ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();

// a named schema. It returns a $ref you can use below.
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema);

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    },
    security: <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'bearerAuth': <String>[]},
    ]);

A schema can be:

  • a JSON Schema Map<String, dynamic>,
  • a dox_validation schema (any object with toJsonSchema()),
  • a JsonSchemaSource.

Paths can use {id} or :id. Both become {id}.

docs.title: 2. Make the document
docs.text:
OpenApi api = OpenApi(
  info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'),
  servers: const <Server>[Server('https://api.example.com')],
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()},
  docs: docs,
);

docs.title: 3. Add the routes you did not describe
docs.text:
DoxRouteAdapter reads the Dox router and adds a basic entry for each route. Routes you already described are not changed.

DoxRouteAdapter(securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
  'AuthMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
    <String, List<String>>{'bearerAuth': <String>[]},
  ],
}).addTo(docs, Route().routes);

Methods that OpenAPI does not know (PURGE, COPY, ...) are skipped.

docs.title: 4. Output
docs.text:
api.toJson();          // Map
api.toJsonString();    // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();          // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi'); // openapi.json + openapi.yaml

// adds the router routes and writes both files
await generateOpenApi(api, 'storage/openapi', routes: Route().routes);

docs.title: 5. Serve it
docs.text:
OpenApiServer returns the body and the content type for /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml and /docs.

OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api);

for (String path in <String>['/openapi.json', '/openapi.yaml', '/docs']) {
  Route.get(path, (DoxRequest req) {
    OpenApiResponse res = server.handle(path)!;
    return response(res.body).contentType(ContentType.parse(res.contentType));
  });
}

Tip

Call DoxRouteAdapter().addTo() after all routes are registered, so it sees every route. Do not serve /docs in production if your API is private.

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
dox_socketio is a Socket.IO server for Dart. The official clients connect to it with no changes: socket.io-client (JavaScript v4) and the Dart socket_io_client package.

Socket.IO or WebSocket?

  • WebSocket (dox_websocket) runs inside the Dox HTTP server. It uses its own small JSON format.
  • Socket.IO (this page) works with the Socket.IO clients. It has acks, namespaces, binary data and long-polling.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_socketio

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.on('connection', onConnection);
  await io.listen(3001);
}

void onConnection(Socket socket) {
  socket.emit('welcome', 'hello');
  socket.join('lobby');
  socket.on('chat', onChat);
}

void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
  event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
  event.ack('ok'); // answer the client callback
}

Client (JavaScript):

import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3001');
socket.emit('chat', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'ok'

docs.title: In a Dox app: same port as HTTP
docs.text:
dox_core can serve Socket.IO at /socket.io/ on the app port. It is off by default.

// config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIo = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: Env.get<bool>('SOCKETIO_ENABLED', false),
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(), // shares broadcasts between isolates
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}

AppConfig(socketIo: socketIo, ...);
  • Requests to /socket.io/ go to Socket.IO before the router. Middleware and body reading are skipped.
  • When it is off, there is no extra work per request.
  • Dox().socketIo is the server of this isolate: Dox().socketIo?.to('room').emit('news', data).
  • dox_websocket (Route.websocket) still works next to it.

Many isolates

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server.

  • Clients should connect with websocket only. One websocket stays on one isolate. With the Redis adapter, a broadcast reaches clients on every isolate.
  • HTTP long-polling sends many requests, and they can reach different isolates. It only works with totalIsolate: 1, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.
const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });

Dox logs this hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.

docs.title: Where to run it (outside Dox)
docs.text:
io.listen(port) opens its own port. Run it in its own small program, for example bin/socket.dart, next to the Dox HTTP server. Put both behind the same proxy.

  • io.attach(httpServer) uses a dart:io server you already have.
  • In your own dart:io server, call io.handle(request) when io.matches(request) is true.
  • The path is /socket.io/ by default.

docs.title: Namespaces in a class
docs.text:
A namespace can be a class. Its dependencies come in through the constructor.

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

  void checkToken(Socket socket) {
    if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
      throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: {'reason': 'bad token'});
    }
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

io.register(ChatNamespace(MessageService()));

When a middleware throws, the client gets connect_error with the message and the data.

docs.title: Node.js to Dart
docs.text:
Node.js Dart socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.args, e.ack(x) socket.emit('e', a, b) socket.emit('e', a) or socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b]) await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5)) socket.join(r) / socket.leave(r) the same socket.to(r).emit(...) the same socket.broadcast.emit(...) the same io.to(r).except(x).emit(...) the same io.of('/chat'), io.use(fn) the same socket.handshake .headers, .query, .auth, .address socket.data socket.data (a Map) io.in(r).fetchSockets() io.to(r).fetchSockets() (this server only)
  • disconnecting and disconnect give the reason in event.data, like transport close or ping timeout.
  • Binary data: send a Uint8List. It can be anywhere in lists and maps.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: ['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: ['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);

docs.title: Many servers: Redis adapter
docs.text:
With more than one server process, use the Redis adapter. Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers.

Redis sub = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: sub, publisher: sub.duplicate()),
);
  • It uses the message format of @socket.io/redis-adapter. A Node.js server can share broadcasts with it, when Node uses a JSON parser.
  • fetchSockets, socketsJoin and broadcast acks only work on the local server.
  • Long-polling needs sticky sessions when many servers share one port. If you can not have them, use transports: ['websocket'] on the client.

docs.title: Storage (dox_storage)
docs.text:
dox_storage gives one API for files on many places: local disk, AWS S3 and S3-compatible services. The API follows FlyDrive and Laravel Filesystem.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_storage for Storage(). In a Dox app, set the disks in config/storage.dart (a StorageConfig), and use Storage(). Storage().use('s3') gives the Disk of this page. Route.files('files') serves local signed URLs. This page is for the full Disk API and for using dox_storage outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_storage

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: Driver Use for Signed download URL Signed upload URL LocalDriver a folder on the server Yes (HMAC with your app key) No S3Driver AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS (HMAC keys) Yes (SigV4) Yes (SigV4) MemoryDriver tests fake URLs fake URLs

docs.title: Set up the disks
docs.text:
DriveManager drive = DriveManager(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, DriverContract>{
    'local': LocalDriver(LocalDriverConfig(
      root: 'storage',
      urlBase: 'https://app.test/uploads',
      appKey: Env.get('APP_KEY'),
    )),
    's3': S3Driver(S3DriverConfig(
      bucket: 'my-bucket',
      region: 'us-east-1',
      accessKeyId: Env.get('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID'),
      secretAccessKey: Env.get('AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'),
    )),
  },
);

Disk disk = drive.use('s3'); // or drive.use() for the default disk

docs.title: Use a disk
docs.text:
await disk.put('avatars/1.png', bytes); // String, List<int> or Stream<List<int>>
await disk.putStream('videos/big.mp4', File('big.mp4').openRead());

Uint8List data = await disk.get('avatars/1.png');
String text = await disk.getString('notes/a.txt');
Stream<List<int>> stream = await disk.getStream('videos/big.mp4');
ObjectMetaData meta = await disk.getMetaData('avatars/1.png'); // size, contentType, lastModified, etag
bool found = await disk.exists('avatars/1.png');

await disk.copy('a.png', 'b.png');
await disk.move('b.png', 'c.png');
await disk.delete('c.png');
await disk.deleteAll('avatars');

ListResult page = await disk.listAll('avatars', ListOptions(recursive: true, limit: 100));
await disk.setVisibility('avatars/1.png', Visibility.public);

docs.title: Save an upload
docs.text:
Stream the upload to the disk. The file is not loaded into memory.

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  await disk.putStream('avatars/${file.filename}', file.stream());
  return <String, String>{'url': await disk.getUrl('avatars/${file.filename}')};
});

Warning

Do not use the file name from the client as it is. Make your own name, for example with a uuid.

docs.title: URLs and signed URLs
docs.text:
String url = await disk.getUrl('avatars/1.png');

// a download link that works for 10 minutes
String signed = await disk.getSignedUrl('avatars/1.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10)));

// the browser can upload straight to S3 with this URL
String upload = await disk.getSignedUploadUrl('avatars/2.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(contentType: 'image/png'));

docs.title: Validation schemas
docs.text:
dox_validation checks data with typed schemas, like Zod. You describe the shape once. You get typed output, all errors at once, and a JSON Schema for free.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_validation for req.validate(), and it exports it. In a Dox app you do not add or import anything: import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' gives v, Schema and the rest. See Validation for req.validate(), validateAsync(), validateSchema() and the unique / exists rules.

docs.title: Install (outside Dox)
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_validation

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
});

// throws ValidationException when the input is not valid
Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

// never throws for bad input
ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}

docs.title: Use it in a controller
docs.text:
class UserController {
  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    // 422 with {field: message} when it fails
    Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);
    // ... save data
  }
}

Or in a form request: return the schema from schema(). A schema.parse() that throws inside a controller also answers 422.

Note

dox_core exports dox_validation without its ValidationException, because dox_core has its own (the HTTP 422 one). dox_orm also has a Schema class. In a file that uses both, import dox_orm with a prefix.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Schema Checks v.string() min, max, length, nonEmpty, email, url, uuid, ip, datetime, regex, startsWith, endsWith, includes, alpha, alphaDash, alphaNumeric, trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase v.int(), v.num() min, max, gt, lt, positive, nonNegative, multipleOf v.bool() v.date() DateTime only. min, max v.enumOf([...]), v.literal(x) v.list(item) min, max, nonEmpty v.object({...}) strict, passthrough, strip, pick, omit, extend, partial v.map(values, keys: ...) any keys v.union([...]) the first match wins v.any(), v.file() file() has image and extensions

On every schema:

  • optional(): the key may be missing. null is still an error.
  • nullable(): the value may be null. The key must be there.
  • nullish(): both.
  • defaultTo(x): the value when the key is missing. (default is a reserved word in Dart.)
  • transform(fn), refine(fn), refineAsync(fn), superRefine(fn), use(rule).
  • describe(text), example(x): only used in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Coercion
docs.text:
Query strings and form data are always text. v.coerce turns text into the right type first.

v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'

docs.title: Checks across fields
docs.text:
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);

docs.title: Async checks
docs.text:
Use refineAsync for a check that needs the database.

final StringSchema email = v.string().email().refineAsync(
  (String value) async {
    return !(await users.emailExists(value));
  },
  message: 'The {field} is already taken',
);

await email.parseAsync('a@dox.dev');

Warning

parse() throws a StateError when a schema has async checks. Use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync() then.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
Extend Rule for a check you want to reuse. Add an extension method, so it looks like a built-in check.

class SlugRule extends Rule<String> {
  SlugRule({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug';
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9-]+$').hasMatch(value);
  }
}

extension SlugMethods on StringSchema {
  StringSchema slug({String? message}) {
    return use(SlugRule(message: message));
  }
}

v.string().min(3).slug();
  • For a database check, extend AsyncRule and implement checkAsync.
  • RuleContext gives path, field, root (the whole input) and lookup('other.field').

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Each error has a code, like required or min_length. Dox finds the message in this order:

  1. The message on the check: .min(3, message: 'Too short').
  2. messages['path.code'], like email.required.
  3. messages['code'], like required.
  4. The default English text.

Placeholders: {field}, {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

// for the whole app
v.messages.setMessages(<String, String>{'required': 'Please fill in {field}'});

// for one call
createUser.safeParse(input, messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
}));

For other languages, extend MessageResolver and override resolve().

docs.title: Rule strings with fromRules
docs.text:
Do you already have rule strings? v.fromRules() turns them into a schema.

final ObjectSchema rules = v.fromRules(<String, String>{
  'email': 'required|email|max:255',
  'age': 'nullable|integer|min:18',
  'nickname': 'sometimes|required|string',
  'address.city': 'required',
  'products.*.name': 'required',
});

rules.parse(req.all());
  • A missing field that is not required skips its other rules.
  • nullable: null is fine. sometimes: skip everything when the field is missing.
  • Each field stops at its first error, so there is one message per field.
  • An unknown rule name throws an ArgumentError when the schema is built.

Add your own rule name:

v.registerRule('unique', (RuleDefinition definition) {
  return UniqueRule(table: definition.arg(0)); // 'unique:users'
});

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text:
Every schema can export JSON Schema (draft 2020-12, the one OpenAPI 3.1 uses). Pass it to OpenAPI to document your API.

v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'email': v.string().email().describe('Login email'),
  'age': v.int().min(18).nullable(),
}).strict().toJsonSchema();

{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email", "description": "Login email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 }
  },
  "required": ["email", "age"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}

docs.title: Standard Schema
docs.text: Every schema implements the Standard Schema interface (StandardSchema). Code that only needs to validate can accept any StandardSchema, from Dox or from another library.

docs.text:
Use auth package in controller to attempt login.

class AuthController {
    login() {
        Map<String, dynamic> credentials = req.only(<String>['email', 'password']);
        Auth auth = Auth();
        String? token = await auth.attempt(credentials);
        if(token != null) {
            User? user = auth.user<User>();
            return user;
        }
        return response("unauthorized").statusCode(401);

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
CORS, or Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, is a security feature implemented in web browsers to control and regulate requests made between web pages from different origins (domains). It ensures that web applications running at one domain are allowed or restricted from making requests to resources (such as data or services) hosted on a different domain. CORS helps prevent potentially harmful cross-site request forgery (CSRF) and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks while enabling safe data sharing and interaction between web applications on separate domains when configured appropriately.

CORS configuration can be found in lib/config/cors.dart

cors.dart 
CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
    /// Enabled
    /// -------------------------------
    /// A boolean to enable or disable CORS integration.
    /// Setting to true will enable the CORS for all HTTP request.
    enabled: true,

    /// Origin
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of allowed origins.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed origins.
    /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request origins.
    origin: '*',

    /// Methods
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Request-Method`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of request methods.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of request methods.
    /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request methods.
    methods: '*',

    /// Headers
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of allowed headers.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed headers.
    /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request headers.
    headers: '*',

    /// Expose Headers
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of expose headers.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of expose headers.
    exposeHeaders: <String>[
        'cache-control',
        'content-language',
        'content-type',
        'expires',
        'last-modified',
        'pragma',
    ],

    /// Credentials
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Toggle `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.
    credentials: true,

    /// MaxAge
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Define `Access-Control-Max-Age` header in seconds.
    maxAge: 90,
);

docs.title: Form data (File)
docs.text:
An uploaded file is a RequestFile. Get it with req.input('image'). The request must be multipart/form-data, with a file field named image.

class ApiController {
    Future<dynamic> uploadImage(DoxRequest req) async {
        req.validate({
            'image': 'required|image:png,jpg',
        });

        RequestFile image = req.input('image');
        String uploadedPath = await image.store('images');

        return {"filename" : uploadedPath};

}

docs.title: RequestFile
docs.text:
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.filename;        // name from the client
file.filetype;        // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension;       // mp4
file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');              // save to storage. returns the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // move it. returns the new File
await file.bytes;     // the whole file in memory. avoid for big files

Save the file before you return

A file up to 1 MB stays in memory. A bigger file is streamed to a temp file while it arrives. The temp file is deleted when the response is sent. So call store, moveTo or stream before your controller returns.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
A body that is too big gets 413 Payload Too Large. Dox checks Content-Length first, and also counts the bytes while reading.

AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in your proxy, like client_max_body_size in nginx.

docs.title: Step 2. Register in app
docs.text:
Register a request in lib/config/app.dart

formRequests: <Type, FormRequest Function()>{
    BlogRequest:() => BlogRequest(),
},

Why?

If we don't utilize dart:mirrors, there isn't a straightforward method to instantiate a class from a string in Dart. Instead, we must register your request class in the app.dart file. As a result, Dox will seamlessly route the request to the corresponding controller.

docs.title: Step 3. Usage
setUp
docs.text: Within this function, you have the opportunity to assign values to variables based on the incoming request, which can then be reused within the controller.

docs.title: rules
docs.text: This function serves as the location for defining validation rules for input requests.

docs.title: messages
docs.text: In this function, you have the ability to configure custom validation messages for input form request validation. Check here for more about validation.

docs.title: schema
docs.text:
Return a dox_validation schema to check the body with typed output. When schema() is not null, Dox uses it instead of rules(). Build it once in a static final field, because schema() runs on every request.

class SignUpRequest extends FormRequest {
    static final ObjectSchema _schema = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
        'name': v.string().trim().min(3),
        'age': v.coerce.int().min(18),
    });

    @override
    ObjectSchema? schema() => _schema;
}

The schema (or the rules()) also becomes the request body in the OpenAPI docs.

docs.title: validated
docs.text:
The checked data, set before setUp() runs. With schema() it is the typed output. With rules() it is the fields that have rules.

store(SignUpRequest req) {
    int age = req.validated['age'];
}

Info

A form request always validates with async support, so unique and exists rules work in rules().

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The response can take various forms, including strings, maps, models, serializers, lists of models, and various types of exceptions.

stringexceptionmap/jsonmodellist of modelfiledownloadstream 
/// string
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        return 'pong';
    }
}

/// exception
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        return InternalErrorException();
    }
}

/// map
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        return {"message" : "hello world!"};
    }
}

/// Model
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        Admin admin = await Admin().find(1)
        return admin;
    }
}

/// List<Model>
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        List admins = await Admin().all()
        return admins;
    }
}

/// File: streamed, with Content-Length and Range support
class VideoController {
    show(DoxRequest req) {
        return File('storage/video.mp4');
    }
}

/// DownloadableFile
class PdfController {
    download(DoxRequest req) async {
        DownloadableFile file = await Storage().download('filename.pdf');

        return file;
    }
}

/// StreamFile
class PdfController {
    download(DoxRequest req) async {
        StreamFile file = await Storage().stream('filename.pdf');

        return file;
    }
}

Info

Models and lists of models will be automatically converted into JSON format and arrays of JSON.

  • Storage().stream() and Storage().download() on the local disk also stream the file.

Upgrade from 2.x to 3.x
docs.text:
3.x is alpha

3.0.0-alpha.1 can still change before the stable release. The 2.x docs stay online: pick 2.x in the version menu at the top.

docs.title: Do these first
docs.text:
1. Use Dart 3.13 or newer.
  2. Set every Dox package to the same version, ^3.0.0-alpha.1. All Dox packages now share one version.
  3. Replace dox_query_builder with dox_orm.
  4. If you use ioredis in your app, update it to ^2.0.0-alpha.1.
  5. Run dart pub upgrade, then dox build_runner:build.
  6. Read the list below. Each item says what breaks and how to fix it.
environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

dependencies:
  dox_core: ^3.0.0-alpha.1
  dox_orm: ^3.0.0-alpha.1        # was dox_query_builder
  dox_migration: ^3.0.0-alpha.1
  dox_auth: ^3.0.0-alpha.1
  dox_websocket: ^3.0.0-alpha.1
  ioredis: ^2.0.0-alpha.1        # only if you use redis

dev_dependencies:
  dox_builder: ^3.0.0-alpha.1
  build_runner: ^2.17.1

// old
import 'package:dox_query_builder/dox_query_builder.dart';
// new
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

Info

dox_query_builder 3.x still works. It only re-exports dox_orm. New fixes go to dox_orm only.

docs.title: Database and query builder
docs.text:
Names are quoted. Table and column names are now quoted ("name" on Postgres, `name` on MySQL). On Postgres a quoted name is case sensitive. If you made a column with CREATE TABLE ... (userId int) without quotes, Postgres saved it as userid. Now where('userId', 1) looks for "userId" and fails. Fix: use the real (lower case) name, or rename the column. For raw SQL use selectRaw and whereRaw.

orderBy checks the direction. A direction that is not asc or desc now throws an ArgumentError. Before, it was put into the SQL. Fix: only pass asc or desc.

toSql() output changed. The where part is wrapped in brackets, and names are quoted. Fix: update tests that compare SQL text.

count() changed. It ignores limit, offset and orderBy. With groupBy it returns the number of groups. Before, it returned the size of the first group.

model.delete() and model.forceDelete() delete only that row. Before, they had no where condition and deleted every row of the table.

forceDelete() also deletes soft deleted rows. withTrash(false) on a model without soft deletes no longer adds a deleted_at filter.

Postgres uses a real pool. Each query no longer runs in its own transaction. Use QueryBuilder.transaction() when you need one.

save() can set a field to null on update. Before, null fields were skipped.

MySQL driver is now mysql_dart (was mysql1).

  • extra['characterSet'] is not read any more. Use extra['collation'] (default utf8mb4_general_ci).
  • TIME columns are now a String (was a Duration).
  • BLOB columns are now a Uint8List (was text).
  • Only JSON columns are decoded to Map/List. MariaDB still decodes JSON-like text.
  • getDatabaseConnection() returns a MySQLConnectionPool.
  • A connection you pass to the migration package must be a mysql_dart MySQLConnection or MySQLConnectionPool.

save(), delete() and forceDelete() return Future<bool>. They return false when a model event cancels them. Code that overrides these methods in a model must use Future<bool>.

A model can not have a field or method named like a model hook. The Model class now has onSaving(), onCreated(), onDeleted() and the other event hooks, plus restore(), saveQuietly(), hasModelHooks and setComputedValues(). Fix: rename a field with one of these names.

dox_builder needs the new analyzer. It uses analyzer 14, source_gen 4 and build 5, so it needs Dart 3.13 or newer. Set build_runner: ^2.17.1 in dev_dependencies. Other builders in your app (for example json_serializable) must also support analyzer 14.

New: computed values with @Computed(), model events and observers, and restore() for soft deleted models.

New: SQLite, whereNull, whereNotNull, whereNotIn, orWhereIn, orWhereNotIn, selectRaw, boolean() column, transactions. See Database.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
Migrations are Dart files now. dox make:migration create_users_table makes a Dart class in db/migration. It also makes the registry db/migration/migrations.dart and, once, bin/migrate.dart. The dox migration:* commands run bin/migrate.dart in your app. Old .sql migrations still run. Use make:migration <name> --sql for a new .sql file. dox migration:status shows which migrations ran.

The runner is renamed. Migration() is now Migrator(). Migration is now the base class of a Dart migration. migrate(conn) is now Migrator(connection: conn).migrate(). rollback(null, 2) is now rollback(step: 2).

The schema builder changed. See Schema builder.

  • Schema.create(...) is now Schema().create(...), or the schema given to up.
  • In schema.table(...) a column is added. Add .change() to change a column that exists.
  • string() is VARCHAR(255) by default. It was 100.
  • id() is BIGSERIAL on Postgres. It was SERIAL.
  • money(), float4() and float8() are removed. Use decimal(), float() or double().
  • foreignId('user_id').constrained() guesses a plural table: users, categories.
  • CREATE TABLE and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX no longer add IF NOT EXISTS. Check with schema.hasTable() first if you need it.

Rollback undoes only the last batch, newest first. Use dox migration:rollback --step=2 for more. migration:reset undoes all. migration:refresh undoes all and runs them again.

A failed migration stops the run. The command throws and the CLI exits with code 1. Each file runs in one transaction.

.sql parsing is stricter. Only lines -- up and -- down start a section. A ; inside quotes, comments or $$ bodies does not split a statement.

The dox_migration executable is gone. Use the dox CLI.

See Migration.

docs.title: Requests and responses
docs.text:
Big uploads go to a temp file. A file over 1 MB is streamed to a temp file. The temp file is deleted when the response is sent. Fix: save the file (store, moveTo or stream) before your controller returns.

Body size limits. A JSON or urlencoded body over 10 MB, or a form-data body over 100 MB, gets 413 Payload Too Large. Fix: raise maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize in AppConfig if you need more.

RequestFile changed.

  • The constructor takes filename, filetype, length, and bytes or file. The stream argument is gone.
  • size is now right: it is the size in KB. Before, it added up the byte values.
  • New: length (bytes), stream(), moveTo(), file.

Cookie Max-Age is in seconds. Before, Dox sent milliseconds, so a 1 hour cookie lived 1000 hours. req.cookie() now returns the decrypted value, and many cookies in one header work.

CORS preflight. An OPTIONS request with no route answers 204 with the CORS headers.

See Request and Response.

docs.title: Server and config
docs.text:
Isolates default to the CPU count (was 3). Each isolate has its own memory. Websocket rooms without a Redis adapter only reach clients on the same isolate. Fix: use the Redis adapter, or set totalIsolate: 1 (or APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1). See Isolate.

Real environment variables win over .env. Before, Env.get() only read the .env file. Now a variable set in the shell or in Docker wins.

gzip is off by default. Turn it on with AppConfig(compress: true), or let your proxy do it.

dox build makes an AOT bundle in build/bundle. The binary is build/bundle/bin/server. It uses dart build cli, not dart compile exe. dox_orm uses sqlite3 v3, which bundles SQLite with a build hook, and dart compile exe stops with "does not support build hooks". If your own Dockerfile or CI runs dart compile exe, change it to dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build and copy all of build/bundle. See Deployment.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
A missing or null field skips its rules. Only required, required_if and required_if_not still run. Before, 'status': 'in:active,inactive' failed when status was not sent. Now it passes. Fix: add required where the field must be sent. Use nullable and sometimes for the other cases.

Validation runs on dox_validation. The messages and the {field: message} error map are the same.

  • An unknown rule name throws when the rules are first used. Before, it logged a warning and was skipped. Fix: correct the name, or add it with v.registerRule().
  • DoxValidator.addCustomRule() still works. For new code, use v.registerRule().
  • req.validate() now returns the validated fields (it returned nothing).
  • dox_core now exports the dox_validation names (v, Schema, Rule, ...). dox_orm also has a Schema class. A file that imports both and uses Schema gets an "ambiguous import" error. Fix: import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' as orm; or hide Schema.
  • A class of yours named like a dox_validation class (for example Validator or Rule) wins in its own file. In other files, hide the dox_core one.

See Validation.

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text: Rooms use the plain room name. Emit to the same name the client sent with joinRoom. room() returns a new emitter and does not stay set for later events.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: attempt() returns null when the email, the password or the stored hash is missing. Before, a login with only a password could match the first user in the table.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Generated names keep word breaks. dox create:controller BlogPost makes blog_post.controller.dart with class BlogPostController. Generated models import package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart.

create:migration is now make:migration. The old name still works. It makes a Dart file by default. --dart is gone, use --sql for a .sql file.

create:model Blog -m makes a Dart migration. The migration is create_blogs_table, and the model gets @DoxModel(table: 'blogs').

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
Cache() runs on dox_cache. The config changed:

// old
CacheConfig(
  defaultDriver: 'file',
  drivers: <String, CacheDriverInterface>{'file': FileCacheDriver()},
);

// new
CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'file',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1'},
  },
);
  • CacheDriverInterface and FileCacheDriver are gone. For your own driver, see dox_cache.
  • Values must be JSON types (Map, List, String, num, bool). Other types throw.
  • put with no duration keeps the value forever. Before, it kept it 1 hour. Pass duration: where you need a limit.
  • Cache().flush() with no tag empties the whole store.
  • Old cache files are not read. The new files are plain JSON, not encrypted. Delete storage/cache once.

See Cache.

docs.title: File storage
docs.text:
Storage() runs on dox_storage. AppConfig(fileStorage:) is now AppConfig(storage:):

// old
FileStorageConfig(
  defaultDriver: 'local',
  drivers: <String, StorageDriverInterface>{'local': LocalStorageDriver()},
);

// new
StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'},
  },
);
  • StorageDriverInterface and LocalStorageDriver are gone. Implement DriverContract from dox_storage and call Dox().storage.register(name, driver).
  • Storage().disk('name') with a name that is not in the config throws. Before, it used the default disk.
  • put, putRequestFile, get, exists, delete, stream and download work as before. Paths still look like /images/<uuid>.png.
  • stream() now gets the content type from the file extension, not from the first bytes.

See File Storage.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
A missing key is never the text "null". Before, Env.get('APP_KEY') with no APP_KEY gave "null", so the app used a key anyone can guess. Now a String gives '', String? gives null, and int, num, double, bool throw an ArgumentError. Fix: give a default where a key is optional, for example Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000).

An empty APP_KEY stops the server in production (APP_ENV=production). Run dox key:generate.

docs.title: New built-in features
docs.text:
• OpenAPI docs at /docs, on by default only when APP_ENV is development or local. dox openapi:generate writes the files.
  • Socket.IO on the app port, off by default.
  • unique and exists rules, validateAsync(), validateSchema() and FormRequest.schema().
  • Route.files() for local signed URLs, and the catch-all route param {path*}.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
req.validate() checks the request data with rule strings, like 'required|email'. When a rule fails, Dox answers 422 with the errors, like {"email": "The email is required"}.

It runs on dox_validation, which is built into dox_core. The rule strings become a schema once (v.fromRules()), and Dox keeps it for the next request.

ValidationRequest body 
class BlogController {
    create(DoxRequest req) {
        req.validate({
            'title': 'required|string|alpha',
            'body' : 'required|string',
            'status' : 'required|in:active,draft',
        });

        ....
    }
}

{
    "title" : "Dartondox",
    "body" : "A perfect solution for your web backend development with dart, a comprehensive and versatile framework that offers a wide range of features to help you build powerful and scalable web applications.",
    "status" : "active",
}

Tip

Multiple rules can be separated by a vertical bar, represented as " | ".

docs.title: Validated data
docs.text:
validate() returns only the fields that have rules. The values are not changed.

Map<String, dynamic> data = req.validate({
    'title': 'required|string',
    'body': 'required',
});

docs.title: Database rules: unique and exists
docs.text:
These rules read the database, so they are async. Use validateAsync:

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateAsync({
    'email': 'required|email|unique:users,email',
    'category_id': 'required|exists:categories,id',
});
  • unique:table,column: no row has this value. column defaults to the field name.
  • unique:users,email,5: ignore the row with id = 5 (for an update). unique:users,email,5,user_id uses another id column.
  • exists:table,column: a row with this value must exist.

They use the default connection of dox_orm. SqlQueryBuilder.initialize() adds them, so they work once the ORM service runs. req.validate() with an async rule throws an error that tells you to use validateAsync. A form request always runs async rules.

docs.title: Typed schemas
docs.text:
validateSchema takes a dox_validation schema and returns its typed output. Use v.coerce for query strings and form data, because they are text.

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
    'name': v.string().trim().min(3),
    'age': v.coerce.int().min(18),
    'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5).optional(),
}));
int age = data['age']; // an int, not '18'

v, Schema and the other dox_validation names come with import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart'. A schema.parse(...) that fails inside a controller also answers 422.

Schema from dox_orm

dox_orm also has a Schema class (the schema builder). In a file that imports both and uses Schema, add a prefix: import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' as orm;.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
Add a rule name for rule strings:

class EvenRule extends Rule<Object?> {
    @override
    String get name => 'even';

    @override
    String get defaultMessage => 'The {field} must be even';

    @override
    bool check(Object? value, RuleContext context) {
        return int.tryParse('$value')?.isEven ?? false;
    }
}

v.registerRule('even', (RuleDefinition d) => EvenRule());
req.validate({'count': 'required|even'});

For a database check, extend AsyncRule and use validateAsync. An unknown rule name throws an error when the rules are first used.

docs.title: Custom validation message
docs.text:
class BlogController {
    create(DoxRequest req) {
        req.validate({
                'title': 'required',
                'email': 'required|email',
            },
            messages: {
                'required' : 'the {field} is required',
                'email' : 'the {value} is not valid email',
            },
        );
    }
}

Info

The validator will automatically substitute {field} and {value} with the corresponding request field and its value.

docs.title: Nested Validation
Nested with array
Optional fields
docs.text:
Changed in 3.x

Before 3.x, all rules ran on a missing field. So 'status': 'in:active,inactive' failed when status was not sent.

A field that is missing, null or an empty string is optional. Its other rules are skipped. Only required, required_if and required_if_not still run.

req.validate({
    'status': 'in:active,inactive', // passes when status is not sent
    'age': 'required|integer', // fails when age is not sent
});

docs.title: nullable
docs.text:
The field may be null. Other rules run only when it has a value.

req.validate({
    'age': 'nullable|integer',
});

docs.title: sometimes
docs.text:
Validate the field only when it is sent. Use it with required to allow a missing field but reject an empty one.

req.validate({
    'name': 'sometimes|required',
});
